summary: Zong Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Gyuto Monastery, and under Trijang Rinpoche and Dechen Nyingpo. He served as abbot of Ganden Shartse and later as director and Rektor of CIHTS.

Specializing in philosophy and sinology, Mou studied at Peking University and under Shili Xiong. He held posts at institutions including West China Union University, National Taiwan University, Tunghai University, CUHK, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

Zorya Nikolayevna Petrunicheva was an Indologist. She graduated in history from Moscow State University around 1943–1948 and became a research fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1953.

Telegdi was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Budapest University of Jewish Studies, Eötvös Loránd University, and under Émile Benveniste. He was later Professor of General Linguistics at Eötvös Loránd University (1958–1979).

Renner is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (MA 1978–1986). She held appointments at Central European University (2014) and, in 2017, at Eötvös Loránd University and the Archaeolingua Foundation.

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gelle studied at Berzsenyi Dániel College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna. She held posts including a fellowship at Eötvös Loránd University and Budapest Centre for Buddhist Studies (2014–2016).

Zuicho Tachibana worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kozui Otani from around 1903 to 1948 and under Edward Denison Ross between roughly 1910 and 1912.

Ito was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (1980–2013) and was a member of the Lotus Sutra institute.
Zuigan Goto was a Buddhist studies specialist. He studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and under Sokatsu Shaku. He later served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Yamaguchi studied at the University of Tokyo, EPHE, and under Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at the CNRS and Toyo Bunko, and was later a professor at the University of Tokyo and Nagoya University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Nakamura studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. In 1945, he became a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University, and he later directed the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Rysiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and under Jerzy Kuryłowicz, Louis Renou, Theodor Bloch, and Émile Benveniste. In 1949, he took a post teaching comparative linguistics at the University of Warsaw.
Gyurme tubten nyinje was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Ármin Vámbéry was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Eötvös Loránd University from 1865 and held a post at Nyugat.

Makaev was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University and Moscow State Linguistic University. He taught at Moscow State University (1938–1960) and served as a professor at the Institute of Linguistics (1954–1976).
Édouard Biot was a sinologist who studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat and Stanislas Julien.

Chavannes was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and Collège de France under Hervey de Saint-Denys and Maurice Jametel, he became a professor at the Collège de France (1893–1918).

Huber worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna, Sorbonne, and under Sylvain Lévi and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and the Sorbonne (1912–1914).

Édouard Lancereau was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf from around 1845 to 1852. He served as a substitute teacher at Lycée Charlemagne and as a proofreader at the Imprimerie Nationale (circa 1856–1884).
